sections.h2: Which government sends an Orlando homeowner the tax statement?
sections.html:
Orange County does. The city levies its own rate, yet the county appraiser sets values and the county Tax Collector mails a single combined statement and takes the payment.

The City of Orlando says it receives about 35 cents of each property tax dollar. The rest goes to Orange County, Orange County Public Schools, the St. Johns water management district and the library system. A seller therefore deals with county offices for everything that touches the bill, and with the city for services, permits and its budget.

  • Orange County Property Appraiser: value, exemptions, mailing address
  • Orange County Tax Collector: bills, payments, delinquent taxes, certificates
  • City of Orlando: sets its own millage rate and budget

sections.h2: How high is the city's own rate?
sections.html:
In its worked example the city prints 0.00665, or 6.65 mills, and says that figure has held for over ten years. The Property Appraiser publishes the final millage for each taxing body by year, so check that site for the current combined rate on a specific address.

A mill is a tenth of a cent on each dollar of taxable value, and the city's rate is only one line on your statement. County, school and district levies add to it, and special assessments sit on top. Ask the Tax Collector for the bill of the property you plan to sell, since the lines vary by neighborhood and by special taxing district.

sections.h2: What does Orlando say about its own finances?
sections.html:
The city's tax page counts over 340,000 residents and says close to 50,000 newcomers arrived within five years. It reports a AAA credit rating from Fitch Ratings and strong reserves, and it reads that the existing 3 percent cap has limited the effect of rising values on long-time homeowners.

For a seller, the figures that matter are practical ones. Roughly six in ten Orlando residents rent, so many buyers of a house here are investors, and the home's tax history is a talking point in any offer. Share the Tax Collector's account page with a buyer, show the exemption status, and mention any special district lines that appear on the bill.

sections.h2: How big is Orlando and who owns homes here?
sections.html:
QuickFacts puts Orlando at 333,888 people in mid-2025, 8.4 percent above the 2020 starting count, on 110.62 square miles. Barely four in ten households own the place they live in.

sections.h2: What are the pay-by dates for an Orlando home?
sections.html:
Statements go out by the start of November, and the last day for the gross amount is March 31. Anyone paying early gets a break that starts at 4 percent for November and shrinks monthly to 1 percent for February. Whatever remains on April 1 is late.

Because the office counts the day money arrives, a letter mailed on March 31 and delivered April 3 is late. Late bills pick up a 3 percent minimum charge and advertising cost, and a certificate auction follows by June 1 with interest bids opening at 18 percent. Escrow customers should note that the lender may hold the bill and the owner may receive only a copy.

sections.h2: What if an Orlando owner disagrees with the assessed value?
sections.html:
File a petition within 25 days of the Notice of Proposed Property Taxes, which the Property Appraiser mails in August. The state revenue department says the petition, one of the DR-486 forms, goes to the clerk of the court.

A denied exemption follows a different clock: a petition to the value adjustment board is due 30 days after the denial letter was mailed. Keep the August notice in your sale file, because it shows the buyer what the county proposes before final rates are adopted in the fall. Public hearings by taxing bodies take place in September and October, and the Tax Collector sends final statements in November.

  • Read the notice the week it arrives
  • Count the 25 days from the mailing date printed on it
  • Ask the Property Appraiser first, since many errors are corrected informally

sections.h2: How do Save Our Homes and the homestead exemption affect an Orlando seller?
sections.html:
Homestead trims taxable value by up to $50,000. Separately, Save Our Homes limits how fast a homestead's assessed value can climb, using the smaller of 3 percent or inflation. The Department of Revenue's chart shows a 2026 cap of 2.7 percent, 2.9 percent for 2025 and 3.0 percent for 2024.

The city's page shows the effect with its sample of a median home bought a decade ago, which stays far below the assessed value of a similar home bought today. A sale ends the protection, since the new owner's assessment jumps to full just value the following January. Sellers who stay in Florida may carry part of the saving to the next home through portability, filed with the exemption application by March 1 and within three years of leaving the old homestead.

sections.h2: Where does the city's slice of the bill go?
sections.html:
The city lists police with more than 900 first responders, fire and rescue with more than 600, 123 parks, 19 neighborhood centers, 900 miles of streets and 1,200 miles of sidewalks. It also reports more than 500 traffic signals.

Those services shape what a buyer sees when touring a home, from park access to street maintenance. The page states that a share of the budget pays for free pools and neighborhood center programs. It also warns that changes to state homestead taxation could reduce city revenue in fiscal years 2028 and 2029. Because the page discusses a statewide property tax amendment on the November 2026 ballot, ask the Property Appraiser or Tax Collector how any approved change applies to your bill before relying on older figures.

sections.h2: How do I deal with open tax balances before listing in Orlando?
sections.html:
Get a written payoff from the county Tax Collector, and plan for any late balance to be wired at the closing. If you ever used the homestead tax deferral, ask the Tax Collector how a deferred balance is repaid at sale.

  • Check whether a tax certificate was sold on the parcel
  • After April 1, pay with certified or cashier's funds, money order or cash in person
  • If two years have passed on an unredeemed certificate, act at once, since a tax deed application can follow
  • Make sure any lender escrow account has paid the current year

A direct cash buyer can often move quickly on a house with a tax lien. Weigh that against listing costs and repairs.

faqs.q: Does Orlando collect its own property tax?
faqs.a: No. The Orange County Tax Collector sends one bill that includes the city's levy. Orlando sets its own millage rate, and the city says it keeps about 35 cents of each dollar paid.

faqs.q: What is the city millage rate in Orlando?
faqs.a: The city's tax page shows 0.00665, or 6.65 mills, and says the rate has been unchanged for more than a decade. Your bill also carries county, school and district levies.

faqs.q: When do Orlando property taxes become delinquent?
faqs.a: On April 1. The full amount is due by March 31, and a payment must reach the Tax Collector by then. A 3 percent minimum charge and advertising cost follow.

faqs.q: Does my homestead cap carry over when I sell in Orlando?
faqs.a: No. A sale resets assessed value to just value the next January 1. You may carry part of the benefit to a new Florida homestead through portability, filed by March 1.

faqs.q: Where do I check my tax bill before listing a house in Orlando?
faqs.a: Search the Orange County Tax Collector's records by owner name, parcel ID or address, and use the Property Appraiser's parcel record for value and exemptions.
